settings.title: Settings
settings.callsign.help: Your amateur radio callsign — used for display only.
settings.grid.help: Maidenhead locator of your QTH (e.g. JO20ev). This determines all propagation calculations.
settings.label: QTH name
settings.license.help: Determines which amateur bands are available and the maximum permitted power.
settings.licensehelp: Controls available bands and max power
settings.power.help: Your actual transmit power in watts. Scores are adjusted relative to a 100W reference.
settings.mode.help: Your primary operating mode. Affects the SNR margin calculation — digital modes tolerate lower power better than SSB.
settings.radio.help: Your transceiver model. Used to give model-specific band-condition settings in the drilldown panel.
settings.antenna_gain.help: Gain relative to a dipole (dBd). 0 dBd = dipole. A 3-element Yagi ≈ +5 dBd.
settings.language.help: Interface language for all labels and tooltips.
settings.colorblind.help: Replaces the red-green score scale with a blue-amber palette safe for deuteranopia.
settings.threshold.help: Minimum score (%) to count a path as 'reachable' in the list views and Opening Soon.
settings.horizonhelp: How far ahead to look for openings
settings.iauregion.help: Determines which band plan is shown in drilldowns. Auto-detected from your grid square.
settings.apidesc: Data sources used for solar conditions
settings.limits.muf: MUF model is empirical, not VOACAP.
settings.limits.vhf: VHF/UHF: line-of-sight/tropo only (no EME, meteor scatter).
settings.limits.dxcc: DXCC centroids are approximate (large entities vary widely).
settings.limits.radio: Radio settings are starting points only.
settings.limits.dx: No real-time DX cluster (GitHub Pages CSP limitation).

setup.first_run: Welcome! Please configure your station location in Settings.
help.muf: Maximum Usable Frequency — the highest frequency that will be reflected by the ionosphere for this path at this time. Bands above the MUF are 'closed'.
help.sfi: Solar Flux Index (F10.7). A daily measure of solar radio emissions at 10.7 cm. Higher values mean a more ionised F-layer and higher MUF.
help.kp: Planetary K-index. A global measure of geomagnetic disturbance on a scale 0–9. Kp ≥ 4 begins to degrade HF paths, especially on polar and low-band paths.
help.greyline: The greyline is the sunrise/sunset terminator. When both ends of a path are simultaneously in this zone, D-layer absorption drops while the F-layer remains active, often producing dramatic DX openings on 40–80 m.
help.dlayer: The D-layer (60–90 km) absorbs HF signals, especially below 10 MHz, when the sun is above the horizon. It disappears at night, allowing low-band DX.
help.hops: Each ionospheric reflection is one 'hop'. Typical single-hop F2 covers ~3500 km. Longer paths need multiple hops, each adding loss.
help.score: Propagation reliability score (0–99%). Combines MUF margin, SFI, Kp, D-layer absorption, greyline, multi-hop loss, and power/mode correction relative to 100W SSB.
help.qrp: QRP means transmitting with low power (typically ≤ 5W). Digital modes like FT8 are ideal for QRP as they have a much lower SNR threshold than SSB.
help.es: Sporadic E (Es) propagation occurs when patches of ionisation form in the E-layer (~100 km), typically in summer at mid-latitudes. It can open 6m and 10m for paths of 1000–2500 km with no warning.
